verdict.rationale: Cloudflare documents a serverless model with no servers, capacity planning, or region complexity, and says Agents scale from deploy-once to tens of millions of instances, which implies the same primitives carry from prototype to scale. A hands-on report of an API reaching production within an hour supports the prototype end. However, no evidence explicitly says core APIs stay unchanged as usage grows. Community-reported CPU time limits (30s free, 15min paid) suggest some workloads may outgrow the model. missing for 10: explicit documentation that apps scale without rearchitecting or plan/platform migration, independent corroboration of large-scale production use on unchanged primitives, clarity on how execution limits affect growing workloads.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on the same core APIs and primitives from prototype through massive scale, without rearchitecting or migrating platforms as usage grows

citations.quote: No servers to manage. No cold starts or region complexity.
Deploy once and Cloudflare runs your agents across its global network, scaling to tens of millions of instances.
no GPUs to manage, no capacity planning
In an hour the API was running in production
